venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Monday 8/17** (MOD: MKZ) Net sales $823 vs a $603 target — 136% of goal on a chill Monday. Every bar seat and booth was filled from 7–9pm, uncharacteristic volume for a Monday. 6 meal deals moved on the day and the CC Old Fashioned was the top cocktail. Food $133. Comps $46.80 (emp discount 50% $24.00, Industry Love $7.40, O4W $2.80, F&F $12.60). 37 guests, $22.23 check average. Opener knocked out all cleaning duties and the closer handled volume well; call-out to buss tables faster. Late-night thunderstorms held down the back half of the night, though some Casi Cello staff hung with the team at EON. BOH cleared the ABK list with quick ticket times and a strong staff meal. No incidents. 86'd/low: liquor order drops tomorrow. Favorite moment: the mid-shift volume bump, unusual for a Monday.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Monday 8/17** (MOD: KE; Chef: JMS) Net sales $1,390 against an $1,127 target — 123% of goal. Slow start that stayed steady all night, with a lot of new faces mixed in with regulars and consistently positive impressions. Christine, owner of Moxie (who handles the majority of the bar's menu prints), came in and expressed gratitude for the business. An uptick around 8pm brought a medium-sized pop; the night closed chill with industry folks and regulars visiting. Three industry guests — two bartenders and a barista — came in for cool classics and were walked to the Lucien Gaudin, which one named his new favorite. Food $122. Comps $75 (5%) from employee and typical industry discounts. 41 guests, $33.91 check average. Danny knocked out ABK in office storage and the kitchen between tickets. 86: High Life. No incidents. Favorite moment: regular Gabe back in with his dog Moose, sharing that the bar has been a positive anchor while he settles into the community — he's planning to bring his whole family next Sunday.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Monday 8/17** (AM MOD: Maggie S; PM MOD: Maggie H & Chef Rachel) Net sales $9,074.91 against a $6,775 target — 134% of goal, roughly $2,300 over the revenue goal. Split: DC/AM $1,484.79, D&C (PM) $7,590.12, Garden/6A n/a. Food $2,325.20. Comps $310. 206 guests (Tock), $44.05 average. AM was quiet after a busy start from Care and Reggie; 86 kombucha, evergreen, sparkling water; low matcha and peach black. PM ran steady with a lot of Rockies/Dodgers gear before and after the game — another Oyster Monday in the books — though Maggie H was pulled onto IRDs for a chunk of service. Kitchen had a chill prep day with Dante and Marv and no big pops; low on wagyu flanks, hot honey, chicken thighs and lime chantilly; 911 on red pepper gel, burger meat/portions, onion jam and walnut pesto; 86 burgers. Events: Day 1 of 3 for Anaconda LLC tomorrow, 15 guests 8am–5pm in Vauxhall, coffee/hot water/creamers set on the Vauxhall bar top for an 8am start; the group stays at the Ramble through Thursday, so expect lobby traffic. Breaks made up, no incidents. Favorite moment: the Maggie Squared crossover.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Monday 8/17** (MOD: Kyler; Chef: Mouse) Net sales $4,026 against a $3,733 target — 108% of goal. Beverage $3,731, food $295. Comps $93.50. 120 covers, $34 check average, 1 large party, 6 solos, zero investor cocktails. Early rain may have crimped sales. Even-keeled start with a lot of 8pm dinner flips and a virtually full room around 9:45pm that emptied out — only three covers between 10:15 and 11:30 before a few stragglers refilled the bar. Heavy date-night composition meant slow drinking (roughly 1.5 rounds) and longer-than-normal seatings that made a not-quite-full room look full; the rail was only sat once. Shoutout to Max for absorbing floor training and applying spirits knowledge on her own tables. One social friction point: a four-top treating the room like a reality show, hiding vapes and barely ordering, eventually asked to leave 45 minutes after close. Kitchen was snacks-only and a few tables left early wanting heartier portions — money left on the table. Top sellers: Rosalie, chips & dip. Back-catalog banger: Whateverest. Door reported a humid, mosquito-heavy but quiet street; largest party was a six-top at open, lots of birthdays, and a good late industry push (Ken from Joyface, Gabriel from the Wayland, Kraig from Amor Y Amargo, Courtney Sheehan). Two no-shows, not charged. Maintenance: mice spotted in the kitchen.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Monday 8/17** (MOD: Mikey & Vic; Chef: Josh) **Emergency early close.** Net sales $1,092 against a $4,167 target — 26% of goal. Marquee $1,092 (food $123); Standing Room $0. Comps $0. 29 guests. A promising start was cut short when drains began backing up in every location — bar, kitchen and standing room. The call was made to close early to get ahead of the plumbing issue: Joe reached plumber Eric who was en route, every upcoming reservation was called, Gracy messaged all guests through SevenRooms, a maintenance sign went on the door, and current guests were softly walked out — everyone was understanding and the building was clear shortly after 8pm. Closing duties were completed. 86 cookies, 6ct pot de creme. No incidents or injuries. More detail expected in the morning on the plumbing resolution. Favorite moment: eating the pre-shucked Oyster Monday oysters so they didn't go to waste. (Note: report date field typed as 2021-08-17; matched to 8/17 by post time.)

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative: **DC — Monday 8/17** (MOD: Josh) Net sales including events $3,001.43 against a $3,773 target — 80% of goal. Marquee bar sales $3,047.97; Garden closed. Food $544. Comps $46.54, no voids. 93 guests, $32.27 per guest (the report's GCA field reads $52.66, which does not reconcile to net sales / guest count — computed figure used here). Extreme heat made for a slow open with the first guest arriving around 5:45pm; business picked up around 8pm and the bar top filled with guests who called out a wonderful experience. Service ran smoothly with good communication and strong food recommendations. Having the kitchen back on Mondays made a large impact — the full food menu was pushed and chicken, cookies and donuts were the biggest hits, with Rassan rocking it solo. Wins: kitchen menu, King Mumbo. To tighten: station resets. No incidents; no-shows charged. Maintenance: garbage disposal isn't cutting on. Favorite moment: D. Darby in the building.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Monday 8/17** (AM MOD: Sam; PM MOD: Justin & Chef Shannon) Net sales $2,825 against a $4,500 target — 63% of goal. Split: Municipal Bar morning $363, Municipal Bar evening $2,291, Sun Club $198, Hot Eye $0. Food $1,235. Comps $308.75. Guests 70 (19 morning, 51 evening, OpenTable). A very quiet morning — no food tours, no large parties, one manageable IRD order, and Madi trained with Sierra on her second shift and tried menu items. Evening was equally quiet: closed again with just one server, an SA, a bartender and a barback; three to four tables sat across the night with no rush and about half the restaurant guests came from the hotel, allowing an early close. Sun Club saw little action with Kyanne opening and Jack closing, most of it at the end. Hot Eye dark. No kitchen notes or 86s, no incidents. Favorite moment: Lex and Drew came in and ate as guests for the first time and had a great time.
